CONCEPT.name: Course idea
CONCEPT.blurb: Your idea for the course is turned into a short, clear summary: who the course is for, what they should be able to do afterwards, and what is out of scope.
CONCEPT.next: CourseForge plans the research the course needs.

RESEARCH_BRIEF.name: Research plan
RESEARCH_BRIEF.blurb: A plan for the research: the questions the course must answer, which kinds of sources count as trustworthy, and how the findings will be organised.
RESEARCH_BRIEF.next: CourseForge carries out the research and records every source it uses.

RESEARCH_DOSSIER.name: Research findings
RESEARCH_DOSSIER.blurb: The research itself: facts, rules and evidence, each linked to the source it came from so it can be checked later.
RESEARCH_DOSSIER.next: CourseForge designs the course structure from these findings.

INSTRUCTIONAL_DESIGN.name: Course plan
INSTRUCTIONAL_DESIGN.blurb: The shape of the course: what learners will be able to do by the end, the order of the sections, and how their understanding will be checked.
INSTRUCTIONAL_DESIGN.next: CourseForge writes every screen of the course.

STORYBOARD.name: Screen-by-screen draft
STORYBOARD.blurb: The full written course, screen by screen: the text learners read, the questions they answer and a description of every picture or diagram.
STORYBOARD.next: CourseForge proofreads and tightens the wording.

EDITORIAL.name: Proofreading
EDITORIAL.blurb: A careful edit of the wording: clearer sentences, consistent terms and no accidental changes to the meaning.
EDITORIAL.next: CourseForge chooses the look of the course.

VISUAL_DIRECTION.name: Look and feel
VISUAL_DIRECTION.blurb: The visual style of the course: colours, fonts and how diagrams are drawn, chosen to suit the subject.
VISUAL_DIRECTION.next: CourseForge puts all the pieces together into one course file.

COURSE_MODEL.name: Assembling
COURSE_MODEL.blurb: Everything written and designed so far is combined into one complete description of the course. This step is automatic and makes no creative choices.
COURSE_MODEL.next: CourseForge builds the course that learners will open.

COURSE_BUILD.name: Building
COURSE_BUILD.blurb: The course is built as a single web page file that works in any modern browser, with no installation. Diagrams are drawn and results tracking is added if you chose it.
COURSE_BUILD.next: CourseForge tests the built course like a learner would.

COURSE_QA.name: Testing
COURSE_QA.blurb: The built course is opened in a real browser and clicked through: every screen, every question, keyboard-only use and accessibility for people with disabilities.
COURSE_QA.next: CourseForge decides whether the course is ready to release.

RELEASE.name: Release
RELEASE.blurb: A final check that nothing serious is still open. If everything passes, the finished course and its reports are saved in the course's release folder. If you chose "ask me once at the end", this is where CourseForge stops for your approval.
RELEASE.next: Nothing more: the course is ready to share with learners.

language.prompt: What language is the course in?
language.help: Type a short language code, for example en for English, fr for French or es for Spanish.

audience.help: Describe the learners in a few words, for example "new warehouse staff" or "nurses on the night shift". Press Enter to skip; CourseForge will work it out from your notes.

review.prompt: How much do you want to check CourseForge's work yourself?
review.help: CourseForge always checks its own work with a panel of reviewers and fixes what they find. You can also ask it to stop so you can read and approve its work. Choosing a level replaces any per-step review settings someone wrote by hand in course.yaml. You can change this later.

options.label: Do it all, then ask me once at the end
options.blurb: CourseForge makes the whole course on its own and stops only once, when the course is finished and tested, so you can check it before it is released. Anything it could not fix is listed for you there. Best when you want to give it your material and come back later.

options.label: Only where it matters (recommended)
options.blurb: CourseForge stops for you at a few key points: after it drafts the screens, and at more points when the subject is high-risk, such as health, safety or law.

options.label: Let me approve every step
options.blurb: CourseForge stops after each of the 11 steps and waits for you to approve it. Slower, but you see everything. It does not change its own work without you: you decide what gets fixed.

options.label: Every step, with the strictest checks
options.blurb: Like approving every step, and every course is also treated as high-risk: stricter research rules (official and current sources, the right country or region) and extra checks, whatever the subject. For regulated or safety-critical training.

options.label: Keep my current custom settings
options.blurb: Someone has already set this up by hand in course.yaml. Leave it as it is.

tracking.prompt: Do you want to keep a record of who completes the course and their scores?
tracking.help: CourseForge can record each learner's name, score, pass or fail, and the date they finished. You can change this later.

options.label: No, don't keep records
options.blurb: Learners take the course and see their own score, but nothing is sent anywhere.

options.label: Yes, my organisation has a training system (LMS)
options.blurb: Choose this if your organisation already uses a system like Moodle, Cornerstone or TalentLMS to assign training. CourseForge makes a file you upload to it, and that system records completions and scores. Learners are not asked for their name.

options.label: Yes, send results to a Google Sheet
options.blurb: Each finished course adds a row to a Google Sheet that you own: name, score, pass or fail, and date. Needs a free Google account and about five minutes of setup. CourseForge gives you step-by-step instructions.

options.label: Yes, on our own results dashboard
options.blurb: Results go to a small results server that CourseForge runs on a computer your organisation controls, with a password-protected web page and a spreadsheet download. You can try it on this computer in ten minutes; for real use it needs someone from IT for about an hour.

identity.prompt: What should learners type in so you know who they are?
identity.help: They type this on the results screen when they finish, just before their result is recorded.

options.label: Their name
options.blurb: Simplest. Two people with the same name will look the same in your records.

options.label: Their name and a staff number
options.blurb: Best for organisations: the staff number tells people with the same name apart.

options.label: Their name and email address
options.blurb: Useful when staff do not have staff numbers.

idLabel.prompt: What do you call the staff number at your organisation?
idLabel.help: This is the label learners see next to the box, for example "Employee number" or "Payroll ID".

sheetUrl.prompt: Paste the web address of your Google Sheet connection.
sheetUrl.help: If you have already done the Google steps, paste the address now: it starts with https://script.google.com/macros/s/ and ends with /exec. If not, press Enter. CourseForge will write step-by-step instructions for you, and you can paste the address later.

trackerUrl.prompt: Paste the web address of your results dashboard.
trackerUrl.help: If your dashboard is already running, paste its address now: it ends with /api/events. If not, press Enter. CourseForge will write step-by-step instructions for you and your IT person, and you can paste the address later.
